battle.name: 居魯士大帝征服巴比倫尼亞
battle.theater: 巴比倫城與幼發拉底河中游
battle.brief: 公元前539年，波斯王居魯士二世在提斯里月十六日前後攻克巴比倫：他不作長期圍城，改以工兵在上游築壩分流幼發拉底河，另以主力在城北斯帕爾牽制巴比倫軍，隨後由河道突入，一夜而陷全城。卡面的斯巴達長矛屬於隨軍希臘僱兵重裝步兵；真正改變戰局的，是攻城工程而非方陣。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries: 公元前539年的幼發拉底河中游，波斯與新巴比倫在河兩岸正面接觸，一場以攻城工程與情報取勝的戰役，就此決定了兩河流域的歸屬。交戰一方是居魯士二世率領的阿契美尼德波斯聯軍：居魯士原為安尚一地的王公，公元前559年先取米底王國，繼而於公元前547年在廷布拉擊敗呂底王克洛伊斯，隨後整合波斯、米底、薩迦、阿拉伯與小亞細亞諸部，兵鋒直指東方的亞述與巴比倫。波斯軍以波斯與米底步兵為主幹，配薩迦弓手、游騎兵，以及數量可觀的希臘與愛奧尼亞僱兵重裝步兵；國王自將中軍，後方由自亞美尼亞高地一路串到蘇薩的驛站接力維繫。另一方是末代國王納波尼德的新巴比倫：他自公元前556年即位，王權由他與其子貝爾沙爾分擔，國政與軍令出自城中的祭司集團，總廟埃薩吉拉與伊什塔爾門象徵王權的合法性。守軍包括城內的步兵與戰車兵、城外在斯帕爾集結的野戰軍，以及專職築壩掘壕的工兵隊。兩河流域的編年史與希臘史料都沒有留下這一役的確切兵力數字，可確定的是居魯士的工兵技術遠勝守方。
countriesEn: The middle Euphrates in 539 BC was where Persian power and Neo-Babylonian power met face to face, and a single campaign decided by engineering and intelligence settled the ownership of the river land. On one side stood the Achaemenid Persian confederacy led by Cyrus II: a prince of Anshan who in 559 BC had first taken the Median kingdom, then in 547 BC defeated Croesus of Lydia at Thymbra, and who now united Persians, Medes, Sakae, Arabs and the peoples of Asia Minor under his banner, with his spearhead turned east toward Assyria and Babylon. The Persian army was built around Persian and Median infantry, supported by Saka archers, light cavalry and a substantial body of Greek and Ionian mercenary hoplites; the king commanded the centre in person, while the rear was held together by a chain of relay stations running south from the Armenian uplands to Susa. The other side was Neo-Babylon under its last king, Nabonidus, who had reigned since 556 BC and who shared power with his son Belshazzar; government and military orders issued from the priestly corporation in the city, and the temple of Esagila together with the Ishtar Gate embodied the legitimacy of kingship. Their defenders included infantry and chariots inside the walls, a field army posted at Sippar outside the city, and corps of engineers specialised in dams and trenches. Neither the Babylonian chronicles nor the Greek accounts preserve an exact figure for the numbers engaged on either side; what is certain is that the Persian engineers were far more capable than the defenders.
people: 居魯士二世是這場戰役唯一的主導者，也是阿契美尼德王朝的奠基者。他並非以蠻力攻城，而是用工程、斷流與僱兵作戰，證明波斯人能運用希臘與兩河流域的技術。巴比倫方面的關鍵人物是末代王納波尼德與其子貝爾沙爾：納波尼德把王室與宗教事業的重心放在阿拉伯沙漠的泰瑪，行前將巴比倫及其軍政委託貝爾沙爾，編年史記他在戰事發生前並不在城中；貝爾沙爾身兼王儲、總督與宗正之職，卻未能組織有效的抵抗。色諾芬《居魯士傳》另立兩位要角：敘利亞總督貝列西斯，以及掌管巴比倫的宦官古納瑞斯，傳說正是他向居魯士指出可以利用上游河渠的破綻。希臘方面還有皮西隆這類居魯士麾下的僱兵士兵，據色諾芬記述，他們在行軍途中第一次近距離看見國王的真容。希臘史家之間的記載也彼此牴觸：克特西亞把巴比倫的統治者寫成女王尼托克利斯，與主流記載相去甚遠；希羅多德則記克洛伊斯在城破後被押往巴比倫求見，卻反被居魯士以禮相待。
peopleEn: Cyrus II was the only driving force of this campaign and the founder of the Achaemenid dynasty. He won the city not by brute force but by engineering, by turning the river and by employing mercenaries, proving that the Persians could make use of Greek and Mesopotamian technique. The crucial figures on the Babylonian side were the last king Nabonidus and his son Belshazzar. Nabonidus had made the Arabian city of Tema the centre of his royal and religious projects and, before the crisis, had entrusted Babylon and its government to Belshazzar; the chronicle notes that the king himself was not in the city when the fighting began. Belshazzar combined the offices of crown prince, governor and chief of the temple administration, yet could not organise effective resistance. Xenophon's Cyropaedia adds two further names: Belesys, the satrap of Syria, and Gounareas, the eunuch in charge of Babylon, who is said to have pointed out to Cyrus the breach that could be used in the upper river works. The Greek contingent appears in the story of Psilon, a soldier in Cyrus's service who, according to Xenophon, saw the king's true face at close quarters for the first time on the march. The Greek authorities also disagree among themselves: Ktesias makes the ruler of Babylon a queen, Nitocris, which is far removed from the received account, while Herodotus has Croesus brought to Babylon after the fall and received with courtesy by Cyrus.
kits: 卡面上的斯巴達長矛是這場戰役中最能代表外來兵器的一件：兩米長的木槍，槍尾包銅套，握在希臘重裝步兵手裡既能平刺，也能架在盾後支撐身體；居魯士麾下的希臘僱兵正是靠這類長矛列在方陣前列作戰，色諾芬描寫軍容檢閱時，特別把希臘步兵的長矛與巴比倫降卒的裝束並列作比較。除了它，波斯軍還有柳條製的大盾、較短的鏟形長矛、斧與投石索，以及薩迦弓手使用的複合弓；巴比倫一方以生皮小盾、彎刀與標槍為主，另有數量不多的戰車。攻城器材才是本役的真正主角：據貝羅索斯經亞歷山德羅·波利斯托的記載，居魯士在城北築起土坡，架上包銅的撞木，又掘壕逼近牆根，並截斷幼發拉底河的水源，使城內供水吃緊；渡軍則靠工兵在上游築壩攔河、造浮橋與舟筏，把後方部隊一段一段送過寬闊的河面。糧秣、攻城器械與隨軍物資全靠幼發拉底河航運與陸上駝隊驛道維持。
kitsEn: The dory on the card is the most telling piece of foreign equipment in this campaign: a two-metre wooden spear with a bronze socketed butt, which in the hands of a Greek hoplite served both as a thrusting weapon and as a support for the shield when the body was braced behind it. The Greek mercenaries under Cyrus fought at the head of the phalanx with exactly this kind of spear, and in his review of the army Xenophon sets the long spears of the Greek infantry beside the equipment of the Babylonian captives for comparison. Beyond it, the Persian force carried large wicker shields, shorter spade-shaped spears, axes and slings, as well as composite bows in the hands of Saka archers; the Babylonians fought with small rawhide shields, sabres and javelins, and had a limited number of chariots. The siege equipment is the true protagonist of the operation. Berossus, as reported by Alexander Polyhistor, records that Cyrus built a ramp against the northern wall, mounted on it rams sheathed in bronze, dug a trench to bring the works close to the defences, and cut off the water coming down the Euphrates, so that the city grew short of water; the army crossed by means of dams raised upstream, pontoon bridges and rafts that carried the troops across the broad river in sections. Food, siege trains and the baggage of the army were all sustained by river transport on the Euphrates and by camel trains on the overland relay road.
tactics: 本役的戰術核心是分進合擊加上河流工程，而非兩軍正面對撞。居魯士的軍隊沿幼發拉底河東岸北上，行至城北約五十公里的斯帕爾一帶與巴比倫的野戰軍相遇；短暫交鋒後，居魯士不急於全軍攻擊，而以部分兵馬纏住對手，主力則轉向下游的渡河點。與此同時工兵隊在上游深谷築壩，掘開堤防，把幼發拉底河的水引入人工渠道，使城西一段主河道變成可涉水而行的淺灘或空床；此舉正合圍城者的意圖——波斯人不但能直接過河，還能讓守方最倚重的天然屏障反過來為自己開路。隨後主力在夜色中自河道方向逼近城垣，從水門一帶突入；城內守軍缺乏統一指揮，未能組成建制的反擊，抵抗很快瓦解。居魯士入城之後並非放任劫掠失控，而是先控制城門、分割敵情，再有組織地搬走神像與財貨；色諾芬《居魯士傳》把整個過程寫成一場以情報與工程取勝的奇襲，而不是寸土必爭的攻堅。
tacticsEn: The core tactic was a pincer combined with river engineering, not a frontal collision between two armies. Cyrus's host moved north along the east bank of the Euphrates and came into contact with the Babylonian field army around Sippar, some fifty kilometres north of the city. After a brief clash he did not press the attack with the whole army: part of his force kept the Babylonians engaged while the main body turned downstream towards the crossing points. At the same time engineers raised dams in the deep valleys upstream, breached the embankments and led the Euphrates into artificial channels, turning the stretch of the main channel west of the city into a shallow fording ground or an empty bed. This served the besiegers' purpose exactly, for the Persians not only crossed the river directly but turned the defenders' most trusted natural barrier into a road for themselves. The main force then approached the walls in the dark from the river side and broke in near the water gates. The garrison, deprived of unified command, could not form an organised counter-attack, and resistance collapsed quickly. Once inside the city Cyrus did not let the sack run wild: he first secured the gates, cut the defenders off from one another, and then moved the statues and treasure out in an orderly way. The whole operation is written up in the Cyropaedia as a surprise won by intelligence and engineering rather than as a grinding siege.
data: 關於數字，可靠的只有以下幾組。時間：巴比倫編年史把陷城之日記為提斯里月十六日，換算為公曆約公元前539年10月12日，此說是通行的考訂結果。城防：希羅多德記巴比倫城牆周長約四十斯塔迪亞，約七點五公里，高約百肘，約五十公尺；幼發拉底河自城中央穿過，把城分成東西兩半，兩岸只靠橋樑相通，牆體與城門的佈局另可由後世的遺址復原與考古報告核對。河工：居魯士的壩址、渠道與土坡沒有留下精確尺寸，但貝羅索斯記載他築坡、安放撞木、截河造渠，色諾芬則描述運兵的舟筏與渡河點，兩者都顯示這等工程須以數千計的工匠方可完成。兵力：兩河流域與希臘的記錄都沒有為此役留下確切的交戰人數，任何具體的兵員數字都屬後人推估，不宜採信。戰利：編年史只說財物與神像被大批搬走，未列數目。
dataEn: As for figures, only a few groups of numbers can be relied on. Date: the Babylonian Chronicle gives the fall of the city as the sixteenth day of Tishri, which converts to about 12 October 539 BC on the Julian reckoning; that is the standard reading. Fortifications: Herodotus describes the circuit of Babylon's wall as about forty stadia, roughly 7.5 kilometres, and about one hundred cubits, roughly fifty metres, high; the Euphrates runs through the middle of the city and divides it into an eastern and a western half, the two joined only by bridges, and the layout of the walls and gates can be checked against modern site plans and archaeological reports on the excavations. River works: no exact dimensions survive for Cyrus's dams, channels or ramp, but Berossus's account of a ramp, of bronze-sheathed rams and of a diverted river, together with Xenophon's description of the rafts and the crossing points, show that works of this scale demanded thousands of workmen. Strength: neither the Mesopotamian nor the Greek records give an exact number of the men engaged, and any specific figure is later conjecture that should not be treated as evidence. Spoils: the chronicle says only that treasure and statues were carried off in bulk, without giving any number.
cause: 戰爭有遠因，也有近因。遠因是居魯士的擴張：自公元前559年滅米底、公元前547年於廷布拉擊敗克洛伊斯之後，波斯聯軍已握有安尚與小亞細亞的資源，下一步便是富庶的巴比倫；克洛伊斯在廷布拉戰敗之後曾想向巴比倫求援，波斯不會容忍呂底與巴比倫聯手。近因是納波尼德的宗教政策：他自公元前556年起把各地神像集中運回巴比倫修復，重修埃薩吉拉大廈，向腓尼基諸城索取神像，又拆毀艾薩努的上殿，朝臣與耶路撒冷居民都受到干預；這套做法削弱了祭司集團對國王的信任，使城市在波斯大軍逼近時缺乏一致的支持。編年史的敘述則更為簡潔：波斯大軍進軍，而國王不在城中。兩個層面疊加，才有了未經圍城、一夜而陷的結局。
causeEn: The war had distant causes and immediate ones. The distant cause was Cyrus's expansion: after taking Media in 559 BC and defeating Croesus at Thymbra in 547 BC, the Persian confederacy controlled the resources of Anshan and of Asia Minor, and the next prize was wealthy Babylon. After his defeat at Thymbra, Croesus had thought of asking Babylon for help, and Persia would not tolerate a Lydian-Babylonian alliance. The immediate cause was Nabonidus's religious policy. From 556 BC he had been gathering the cult statues of the empire back to Babylon for restoration, rebuilding the great temple Esagila, demanding statues from the Phoenician cities, and pulling down the upper shrine of Esanna; courtiers and the inhabitants of Jerusalem alike were caught up in it. Such measures weakened the trust between king and priesthood, so that the city offered no united support when the Persian host drew near. The chronicle states the matter more tersely: the great army of the king of Persia advanced, and the king was not in the city. The two layers together produced a city that fell in a single night without a siege.
impact: 新巴比倫王國就此終結，巴比倫編年史的敘事在公元前539年戛然而止，兩河流域進入長達兩個多世紀的波斯時期。居魯士入城後受到祭司集團迎接，被接納為巴比倫的合法君主與馬爾杜克神廟的維護者；這位居魯士圓柱現藏大英博物館，銘文以古巴比倫語寫成，敘述其戰勝、平反被指控的巴比倫人、歸還被掠走的神像並資助各城聖殿，因其自稱以信義治民，後世常把它稱為最早的權利宣言之一。巴比倫城本身並未因易主而衰敗：它繼續是阿契美尼德帝國的西都與總督駐地，聖巴比倫的官署、泥板文書與天文觀測傳統延續下來。宗教層面亦有深遠影響：馬爾杜克神像重回埃薩吉拉，與此同時，第二以賽亞書把征服者寫成受膏者的段落，被後世連結到神像歸位這一政治事實上，逐步成為猶太傳統中異邦君王作為解放者的原型。
impactEn: The Neo-Babylonian kingdom ended there, the narrative of the Babylonian Chronicle breaks off sharply in 539 BC, and Mesopotamia entered a Persian period lasting more than two centuries. Cyrus was received by the priesthood and accepted as the lawful king of Babylon and as the maintainer of the temple of Marduk. The Cyrus Cylinder, now in the British Museum, is inscribed in Akkadian and tells of victory, of setting right the wrongs done to the Babylonians, of returning the seized statues and of endowing the sanctuaries; because it presents the king as ruling by justice, it has often been called one of the earliest declarations of rights. Babylon itself did not decay with the change of masters: it remained the western capital of the Achaemenid empire and the seat of its satrap, and the bureaucracy of Babylon, its clay tablets and its astronomical tradition carried on. The religious consequences were no less far-reaching. The statue of Marduk returned to Esagila, and the passage in Second Isaiah that calls Cyrus the anointed one has been linked by later scholarship to the political fact of the statue's restoration, gradually becoming in Jewish tradition a prototype of the foreign king as deliverer.
result: 巴比倫陷落，城門由居魯士的聯軍控制，貝爾沙爾在城破時陣亡，納波尼德則遭到搜捕；後世傳說稱他最後為居魯士所擒，待遇頗為優厚，未遭加害。巴比倫的財富、軍械與神像落入波斯之手，納波尼德苦心重建的宗教秩序就此終結，馬爾杜克崇拜回到埃薩吉拉的正統地位。居魯士於公元前530年陣亡於中亞瑪吉安的一次戰役，但阿契美尼德王朝對巴比倫的統治延續下去，波斯君主自此以巴比倫之王的頭銜，與兩河流域的祭司集團維持長期合作，也把這座城市納入橫跨三洲的帝國版圖。對後世而言，這一夜既是兩河政治權柄的更替，也是古典世界最早被記錄下來的一場以工程戰與情報戰取勝的攻城實錄。
resultEn: Babylon fell, the gates passed into the hands of Cyrus's confederacy, Belshazzar was killed in the sack, and Nabonidus was hunted down; later legend has it that he was finally taken alive and treated with notable courtesy rather than put to death. Babylon's wealth, its arms and its statues fell to the Persians, the religious order that Nabonidus had laboured to rebuild came to an end, and the cult of Marduk was restored to its rightful place in Esagila. Cyrus died in 530 BC in a battle in Margiana, but Achaemenid rule over Babylon endured: from then on the Persian kingship, styling itself king of Babylon, maintained a long working relationship with the Mesopotamian priesthood and folded the city into an empire spanning three continents. For later ages this single night was both a change of political power in the river land and one of the earliest recorded cases of a siege won by engineering and intelligence.
